question_text: Find the parametric equations of the circle x² + y² + 6x + 8y − 96 = 0.

insider_note: The radius is 11 because 9 + 16 + 96 = 121 — a large negative constant is what makes a big circle, and checking that the sum is a perfect square is a quick check against a sign slip.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Centre and radius
steps.margin_note: One mark. Both linear coefficients are positive, so both centre coordinates are negative.
steps.memory_tip: Halve 6 and 8 to get g = 3 and f = 4, then change both signs.
steps.why: The centre is (−g, −f), so positive linear coefficients put the centre in the third quadrant. Subtracting c = −96 adds 96, and 9 + 16 + 96 = 121 is a perfect square.
common_mistakes: Computing √(9 + 16 − 96), which has no real value.

steps.label: Write the parametric equations
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The centre coordinates go in unchanged; only the radius multiplies the cosine and sine.
steps.memory_tip: x = −g + r cos θ and y = −f + r sin θ.
lines: x = −g + r cos θ,  y = −f + r sin θ

lines.text: ∴ x = −3 + 11 cos θ,  y = −4 + 11 sin θ

steps.why: Every point on the circle is the centre plus a step of length 11 in the direction θ. The centre appears as the constant part and the radius as the multiplier.
common_mistakes: Writing x = 3 + 11 cos θ by using g instead of −g.
Swapping cosine and sine between the two equations.
